## Forecast pipeline

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[Daily buoy observations\n+ water covariates] --> B{Today's state:\nBloom or Calm?}
    A --> C[Per-covariate Random Forests\ntemp, salinity, conductivity, air temp]
    C --> D[Recursive covariate forecast\n7 days ahead]

    B -->|Bloom| E[Bloom-branch Random Forests\npeak magnitude, duration, decline rate]
    B -->|Calm| F[Calm-branch Random Forest\nday-to-day change]

    D --> E
    D --> F

    E --> G[Build trajectory:\nrise to predicted peak,\nthen decline]
    F --> H[Recursive day-by-day\nchlorophyll forecast]

    G --> I[7-day chlorophyll forecast]
    H --> I
```

Every model here is retrained from scratch each day on all historical
data up to that point -- nothing is persisted between days except the
growing observation record and each day's forecast output. Water
conditions (temperature, salinity, conductivity, air temperature) are
forecast forward first, since the chlorophyll models need them as
inputs beyond today. Which chlorophyll model runs depends on whether
today's chlorophyll is currently above or below the bloom threshold:
a bloom in progress uses three Random Forests trained only on
historical bloom events, each predicting one property of how the
bloom will play out (how high it will peak, how many more days it
will last, and how fast it will decline afterward); a calm day
instead uses a single Random Forest that recursively predicts each
day's change from the day before.
